items.title: I Come In Peace
items.summary: As you make your way through this. Through what? Life. Oh.
items.content_html:
As you make your way through this.

Through what?

Life.

Oh.

You attach yourself to certain things.

Like sports teams.

Clicks.

Apparel brands.

Political parties.

Nation-states.

Interests.

Hobbies.

Avocations.

Vocations.

Why?

Most of us do it because it aligns with, or at least represents, a part of us.

It becomes a part of who we are.

There's also some of us who do it because they think it's cool.

Or makes them noticeable.

This is usually folks who, by themselves, would not necessarily be so.

He's talking about luxury watch lovers.

Go Timex!!!

Here's the thing, though.

I'm learning something.

About time.

I'm learning that this is all meant to divide us.

To keep us busy fighting.

Go Giants!!!

See?

As I go up, hopefully I go up, I see that it's all a bit crazy.

I see the world.

And it looks small.

With pockets of fights amongst all the pockets of lights.

Everywhere.

Me?

I'm above it all.

Looking for aliens.

🛸

Up here.

Starfaring.

💫

Seeing if they wanna rumble.

👽

Or if they're down.

items.title: I'll Always Love You Before I Met You
items.summary: I have this annoying habit. Just the one? Where I like…
items.content_html:
I have this annoying habit.

Just the one?

Where I like to sing songs by artists I don't particularly like.

Taylor Dayne, for instance.

Nothing personal, TD.

Just not for me.

But do I like to sing one of her songs now and again.

So I guess it is.

Savage Garden.

🎵 I knew I loved you... 🎶

Not the whole song mind you.

Just the parts that are funny.

The magic is when it gets into my wife's head.

Why am I singing this? Were you singing it earlier?

Why yes.

Yes, I was.

Tee hee.

😊

Whooo whooo hooo hoooh oooh hoooooooh heyyy heyyy heyy.

items.title: Toys R Us Kids
items.summary: One of the interesting things about life is how much I…
items.content_html:
One of the interesting things about life is how much I thought adults had it figured out.

At least, I thought that as a child.

Look at that old dude.

He old.

That man looks like he been through some sheet.

Sweating wisdom.

Instead, many of us old(ish) folk are just kids dressed up in wrinkled clothing.

Hobbies that used to be for kids are now for them all growns up.

And they ready to Venmo.

Video games.

Blocks and figures.

Trading cards.

Traditionally for kids, but now dominated by adults.

They'll fight you (to some degree) in the aisles.

Pretty big industries catering to these kidults.

Yes, that's a term.

And yes, I just learned it.

As a boy, I thought sports cards were fun.

As a man, I reel at the numbers some cards are fetching at auction.

What are we buying here?

A rectangle of cardboard?

Doesn't seem that would be worth much.

Partial ownership of a famous athlete?

That sounds like slavery.

Our youth?

Ouch.

I don't quite understand the allure of it all.

To make money, sure.

But there's something else there.

This market of adults buying stuff that used to be for kids is gigantic.

I don't think a lot of us want to grow up.

And as a former child myself, I understand that part of it.

Not wanting to grow up.

I will leave my conclusion open, because I really don't want to sheet on it.

You do you.

After all.

It's your time.

Spend it how you wish.

Maybe that's the part I wrestle with.

It feels a lot like gambling.

And as an asymmetric bettor myself, you'd think I'd be into that.

But I'm not.

At least I don't think I am.

And that's the part that is interesting.

I used to love GI Joes.

Video games.

Cardboard and inch thick lucite.

But I don't anymore.

I thought I'd have it all action figured out by now.

Pew pew.

items.title: This Is Not Entertaining Advice
items.summary: There's this line. It's kinda hazy. Fuzzy. Opaque. Thick. Now more…
items.content_html:
There's this line.

It's kinda hazy.

Fuzzy.

Opaque.

Thick.

Now more than ever.

And that line separates entertainment from advice.

Entertainment           |||||           Advice

This is not financial advice.

Is what you'll hear.

Then you'd get an hour of financial advice.

Maybe more.

But here's the thing:

Treat what you see online as entertainment.

All of it.

Even, and especially, advice.

The list of people who entertain you can be, and probably should be, limitless.

But the people you heed must be few.

You can, and must, watch folks and just enjoy their schtick.

But for a large part, it's acting.

Playing a part.

Listen to their entertainment.

Don't listen to their advice.

They're aren't giving you it, remember?

This is not legal advice.

A lot of these people, their entire livelihood is centered around talking to a phone.

Or a laptop.

Don't we all do that?

Now like all rules, there are exceptions which prove it.

So exceptionally choose the advice and advicers advisors you follow.

There might be an entertainer out there dropping wisdom, but mostly they are just there to amuse you.

Or infuriate.

Maybe a mix of both.

Please don't take it as gospel.

And for the love of God, don't make any calls that would greatly affect your life based on something or someone you find entertaining.

But I'm just a dude talking through a keyboard.

This musings column is just for entertainment.

My own.

If you like it, sweet.

If not, I get it.

I get it.

Not for everyone.

But remember this last piece of advice:

I'm not giving you any.

items.title: Mind Your Own Beeswax
items.summary: Mind your own business. You ever hear that? It's how I…
items.content_html:
Mind your own business.

You ever hear that?

It's how I grew up.

How I was raised.

Worry about you and yours.

Mouth shut.

And I know that's the city in me.

But it's worked.

For me.

At least I think it has.

People are confounded as to how I can just go on musing about nonsense when the entire world is quite obviously going to sheet.

It is?

But here's the thing.

I don't think it is.

Or at least, at a faster or higher rate than it's always been.

I think we just have access to more people's businesses.

Doomscrolls on the can's worth.

That is a lot.

So we can and often do mind them far more than was ever possible before.

It's a good way to feel wonderful about yourself.

If you're into that.

And a good way to feel bad about yourself.

If you're into that.

Me?

I mind my business.

Someone's got to.

You think these bills pay for themselves?

They don't?

Huh.

🐝🍯🕯

items.title: Gone Fishing
items.summary: Ayy seki. Who's knocking on the door? Ayy seki. What? What…
items.content_html:
Ayy seki.

Who's knocking on the door?

Ayy seki.

What?

What do you want?

Better be dropping off something.

Something with one of them battery sticker warnings on the box.

That means it's something good.

Or food.

Food would be nice.

Oh no.

It's one of them seekers of knowledge.

I can tell because they're squirmy and anxious.

Hat in hand.

Bright eyed.

Can't see their tail but I'm betting it's bushy.

They keep looking for a master.

Some old wise guy.

I'm only one of those.

Two max.

The thing I learned is, if you don't answer the door, they eventually go away.

Probably not the best strategy for a guy selling something.

Wonderful strategy for me.

Yes!

They're leaving.

Yup.

I was right.

Bushy.

items.title: Now That's A Thinker
items.summary: I admit it. I think a lot. Now, some fools out…
items.content_html:
I admit it.

I think a lot.

Now, some fools out there will try and convince you that thinking isn't action.

But it is.

It's an action.

Patience, planning, and strategy sometimes confuses those who just jump at the first shiny object then the next.

Then the next.

Squirrel!!!

🐿

Why are we doing this?

That's a fine question.

How are we doing this?

Finer.

What are we doing?

Best question yet.

Who and when are probably something to consider, too.

All require thinking.

Thinking is an action.

People in this hustle culture or whatever the heck we call it today just brag about how they did this or that but they never stopped to think.

They just kept doing this or that.

That or this.

Look how great I turned out, is their schtick.

But I think, they turned out terribly.

At least for me.

For me.

Not the right fit.

You do you.

I don't want what they have or they claim they got.

I seek something different.

I live something different.

I don't have many heroes, but they all seem to do a lot of contemplating.

Which is just a fancy word for thinking.

Alright stop.

Collaborate and listen.

What are you doing?

Right now.

Why are you doing it?

How are you doing?

Who are you doing it with and for?

When will you decide to do something else?

Do you think it's a good idea?

Do you like your answers?

What are you going to do about it?

items.title: Horizontal
items.summary: Algorithms, man. Algorithms. It occurs to me that I let them…
items.content_html:
Algorithms, man.

Algorithms.

It occurs to me that I let them feed me.

Too much.

Like I'm reclining.

And they got grapes.

🍇

I must admit, I like when they feed me a small creator I never heard of.

Talking about a subject I've been digging into.

One with a small, but dedicated, following.

It's like finding a small town's genius.

The internet can be staggering.

Bigger than any city in the land.

But it's also full of all these tiny, hidden, communities.

Not sleepy at all, though.

Quite lively really.

More my vibe.

I've watched and followed these for a while now.

Marveling at how they don't seem to grow.

They don't change.

And they're fine with it.

Maybe not happy, but fine with it.

I wonder how these people got here.

I wonder if they were fed grapes like me.

The internet, people say, has died.

But they don't know sheet.

Never have.

All of this to say, don't let it feed you forever.

Start using them fingers to type.

Search.

Query.

Hunt.

Type in something and write .com and go there.

See what happens.

Although that sounds like a lot of work.

Fine, fine.

Are those fresh figs?

Lay off me, I'm starving.

items.title: Cherish Is The Word I Use To Describe
items.summary: Man. I wrote a few drafts but erased 'em. I tried…
items.content_html:
Man.

I wrote a few drafts but erased 'em.

I tried to dig deep.

But didn't like what I struck.

So I shoveled it back.

Leveled the ground. 

Couldn't even tell I dug.

Life is this dance between nostalgia and vision and the ever present.

All happening at once.

Past, present, future.

All three are very real, though.

Which is the realist?

Realest.

I used to always think in the future.

Never the past.

But it occurs to me, that perhaps there's more past than future.

At least for me.

And thus I have a lot to look back upon, rather than look forward to.

But I do.

I look forward to a lot.

It's what long game players do.

Even old(ish) ones.

I wear my future lens with the knowledge that every good moment or not so good I get the privilege to experience is because I'm still here.

Because I still walk the earth.

The honor of life.

Of living.

Cherish every second.

As a husband and father, sometimes I just want peace and quiet.

As a husband and father, I know sometimes that's just a pipe dream.

So I take chaos and loudness.

And embrace them.

Give them both a big kiss.

And say, thank you, God.

For headphones.

And all the other stuff.

In between.

Now, shhh...

items.title: Had Me @ Heads Carolina
items.summary: You want to create a hit? What's that now? A hit…
items.content_html:
You want to create a hit?

What's that now?

A hit song.

Top 40 or whatever the metric is these days.

The hard way is to come up with something original.

The easy way is to take an old hit.

Just take it.

Either remake it.

Or make a new song with the old song inside it.

Featuring a 90s 2000s star.

Like Hootie Darius or Jo Dee (Messina, not Dumars - both legends, though).

Talk about Carolina beaches.

Gotta be Carolina.

And falling in love.

It'll be a hit.

I guar-on-tee.

It's pandering.

Lowest common denominator.

You say.

Yes, yes, I suppose it is.

Low hanging fruit.

But nostalgia renewed, man.

Holy crap, do I dig it.

A time machine.

Forwards and back.

I like those.

You want to make a hit?

Look behind you.

You had me at Hootie.

And the hits just keep on comin'.
